document.title: Scenesetter for Your Visit to Islamabad: Afghan Angle (Islama 00436)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Confidential] Background for Robin Raphel's visit. A Taliban government in Kabul would be 'as good as it can get' for Pakistan. The Taliban let HUA use Khost camps, Pakistani aid is 'more significant and probably less malign than most imagine', and Islamabad plays an overbearing role in Taliban political and diplomatic initiatives.

events.description: US Embassy Islamabad sends scenesetter cable for A/S Raphel's visit
UN working group of second-tier faction leaders meets two days in Islamabad; agrees to refer limited prisoner exchange to leaders
Taliban take Kabul and execute Najibullah
Taliban battles with Massoud since September cost Massoud heavy equipment, territory and taxing power.
Massoud captured Taliban and Pakistani prisoners in last fall's fighting north of Kabul.
UN working group of second-tier faction leaders met for two days in Islamabad and agreed to refer a limited prisoner exchange to their leaders and meet again next month.
US Embassy Islamabad sends scenesetter cable for Assistant Secretary Raphel's visit, with talking points on peace process, counterterrorism, narcotics, human rights and pipelines.
Najibullah executed by the Taliban and his corpse hung from a Kabul street pole.
Burhanuddin Rabbani declared jihad against Dostam.
Massoud's battles with the Taliban begin, leading to losses of equipment and territory.
Massoud captured several hundred Taliban and several dozen Pakistani prisoners in fall fighting north of Kabul.
UN working group session in Islamabad; Taliban refused a Ramazan ceasefire but pursued prisoner exchange; Massoud sent a representative.
Mullah Omar warned Taliban soldiers they would be beaten for abusing citizens in Kabul.
Embassy Islamabad sends scenesetter cable for Raphel's visit.

key_claims: The Taliban are the most significant political and military force in Afghanistan, ruling Kandahar easily but acting as an occupying force in Kabul and Herat.
Radical Islamic governments and organizations are approaching the Taliban, with Usama bin Ladin enjoying Taliban hospitality.
Pakistani aid to the Taliban is mostly political, diplomatic and trade-based rather than large-scale military aid, per the embassy.
Pakistan is the only country to definitely recognize the Taliban government.
The Taliban let HUA use camps in Khost, lending credence to Pakistani expectations of a friendly Kabul.
Massoud is weakened and dependent on Dostam, while ISI has reestablished contact with him.
Massoud holds hundreds of Taliban prisoners and perhaps dozens of Pakistanis, driving Taliban prisoner-exchange interest.
